decision: One ownership correction required before integration; otherwise requested three failure-flow cases are represented

findings.problem: terminate sends SIGKILL to -child.pid whenever !passed, even after child exit/close. Assertions after await closed can fail, invoking t.after and signaling a PGID for which this process generation is no longer confirmed. Late-root-removal mutant specifically exercises such an after-close assertion failure.
findings.required: Only signal the still-owned running process generation; stop signaling after observed exit as well as close (track exit or check exitCode/signalCode plus terminal). On unconfirmed/terminal generation retain evidence instead of blindly using stale pid. Preserve real child/IPC barriers and all original oracles.

positiveSourceFindings: Nested real node:test timeout is identified by exact failureType/message while expected nested exit1 is retained; parent does not turn arbitrary errors into positive pass.
Timeout-clean observes body/stop/child barriers separately and requires root present at actual close, removed only after completed nested process.
Stop failure inspects preserved cause tree for FILES_RETAINED, SHUTDOWN_FAILED and both sentinel errors.
Disposal-timeout-late uses unchanged10000ms helper bound, waits precise failure before releasing child, then checks retained root after actual close and nested process exit.
Reporter serializes nonenumerable causes/AggregateError errors; complete lines must parse; strict unhandled-rejections and uncaught monitor prevent silently swallowed promise failures.
Controls target actual helper early deletion and late-inner deletion, with exact source hashes/unique anchors. Controls remain unexecuted and require intended filesystem assertion failures.
Existing helper and original cluster command unchanged; new separate maintained ownership command added.
limitations: Observed helper ownership is not production process ownership acceptance.
Keep failed gate artifacts on failure; fix stale-PGID cleanup before running negative controls.
